about: Lesson A6 (a06-interconnection). Data centers appear only as loads. Real numbers carry their source and date in 'facts' and 'sources'. Illustrative: Prairie Town's cluster of four generator requests, the line headroom, the upgrade and its cost, each project's impact factor and the most it would pay, the 150-day length of every restudy round, the east substation's two lines, the east side's peak and the proposed 300 MW data center campus. The money ledger uses case file CF7's toy unchanged (cf7-cost-of-waiting.json, 'idea': a 100 MW load, invented round numbers, not the study's inputs, equations or results); this file adds only the starting wait and the staged-service extension.

tracks.name: Ridge wind farm, 200 MW
tracks.note: A generator: the federal pro forma rules of Order 2023 (grid operators adapt them).

stages.name: Request
stages.what: Files an [[interconnection-request|interconnection request]] in a 45-day window, with a study deposit based on its MW and [[site-control|control]] of 90% of its site.

stages.name: Cluster study
stages.what: After a 60-day customer engagement window, a [[cluster-study|cluster study]] of every request in the window together: which lines each project would overload.

stages.name: Upgrades and shares
stages.what: Names the [[network-upgrade|network upgrades]] and splits their cost by each project's impact on the overloaded line.

stages.name: Restudy
stages.what: Projects whose share is too high withdraw; the rest are restudied and their shares change.

stages.name: Agreement
stages.what: Signs the [[interconnection-agreement|interconnection agreement]] and posts a deposit of 20% of its network upgrade costs.

stages.name: Building
stages.what: Builds the plant while the utility builds the upgrades; permits, equipment and crews set the pace.

stages.name: Operation
stages.what: Starts commercial operation. For projects built in 2025, the median wait from request to here was over five years.

tracks.name: Data center campus, 300 MW
tracks.note: A large load: rules differ by utility and state; Prairie Town's steps are illustrative.

stages.name: Request
stages.what: Asks the utility for 300 MW of service. In ERCOT's 2026 batch study, a large load posts $50,000 per MW of security.

stages.name: Load study
stages.what: Can the network carry 300 MW with any one line out ([[n-minus-one|N−1]])? Voltage and stability are checked too.

stages.name: Upgrades and who pays
stages.what: A third line into the substation. The [[large-load-tariff|large-load tariff]] decides what the campus pays and what other customers carry.

stages.name: Contract
stages.what: A service contract: a minimum bill, a term and collateral, as lesson A4 sets them.

stages.name: Staged service
stages.what: 200 MW fits on the two lines that exist; the last 100 MW waits for the third line.

stages.name: Building
stages.what: The line and substation work. In this lesson the full 300 MW waits three years.

stages.name: Energized
stages.what: [[energization|Energization]]: power flows. What the wait cost, and whom, is step 9.

cluster.line: the 345 kV line from Wind Ridge into Prairie Town

facts.what: Median time from interconnection request to commercial operation for U.S. projects built in 2025, where data exist.
Share of the capacity that asked to connect in 2000–2020 that was operating by the end of 2025; about 75% withdrew and 10% is still waiting.
Generation and storage actively seeking interconnection in the U.S. at the end of 2025, in about 8,200 projects.

Length of a cluster study in FERC Order 2023's pro forma rules (issued 28 July 2023), after a 45-day request window and a 60-day customer engagement window; facilities and affected-system studies come on top, and restudies follow withdrawals.
facts.source: MISO, FERC Order No. 2023: An Initial Review, slides 3 and 5

facts.what: Large loads seeking to connect in ERCOT, with requested dates through 2033, about 90% of them data centers; ERCOT's highest demand so far is about 91.1 GW.
facts.source: ERCOT to the Texas Senate, slide 6; ERCOT demand records
facts.asof: requests as of June 2026; peak 91,134 MW on 22 July 2026, preliminary

facts.what: Financial security a large load posts in ERCOT's first batch study, which is to give each project MW allocations year by year for 2028–2032.
facts.source: ERCOT to the Texas Senate, slides 3–5

rungs.label: Requested
rungs.text: A request is filed, with a deposit.

rungs.label: Studied
rungs.text: The grid operator has studied it and named the upgrades.

rungs.label: Agreement signed
rungs.text: An agreement is signed and security posted.

rungs.label: Under construction
rungs.text: The plant or load and its upgrades are being built.

off.label: A forecast is not on the ladder

items.text: ERCOT's list of large loads seeking to connect totals 474.7 GW.
items.note: Mostly requests: 284.3 GW had no studies submitted and 5.9 GW were energized (ERCOT, June 2026).

items.text: About 2,061 GW of generation and storage sat in U.S. queues at the end of 2025.
items.note: Queued projects, studied or not yet: the queue is not a forecast. Berkeley Lab counts 1,312 GW plus 749 GW.

items.text: About 549 GW had a draft or signed interconnection agreement but was not yet operating.
items.note: A draft agreement follows the studies; a signed one adds security. Neither is a plant that runs (Berkeley Lab, end of 2025).

items.text: The campus signs a contract with a minimum bill and posts collateral.
items.note: Signed and secured, but nothing is built yet.

items.text: A utility says it expects 3 GW of new data centers by 2030 (an invented example).
items.note: An expectation of loads that are not on the ladder yet; ask how many have signed anything.
